title: Development of a Digital Narrative Learning Model Based on Social Emotional Learning Using Interactive Flat Panel for Bullying Prevention in Early Childhood Education
abstract: Background. Bullying prevention in early childhood education requires structured, concrete, and developmentally appropriate learning experiences that help children recognize emotions, understand peers’ feelings, and choose prosocial actions. Social Emotional Learning (SEL) provides a relevant pedagogical foundation for strengthening anti-bullying behavior, while Interactive Flat Panel (IFP) offers opportunities to present visual, narrative, and interactive digital learning activities. Purpose. This study aimed to develop a digital narrative learning model based on Social Emotional Learning using Interactive Flat Panel and to examine its feasibility, practicality, and initial effectiveness for bullying prevention in early childhood education. Method. This study employed a Research and Development design using the ADDIE model. The analysis stage involved a needs survey of 47 kindergarten teachers, initial classroom observations, and interviews with teachers and parents. The limited implementation trial involved 95 children and 5 teachers from five kindergartens in West Java, Indonesia. The developed model was supported by digital flashcards, animated videos, digital storytelling, digital board books, and educational games. Data were collected using expert validation sheets, teacher response questionnaires, learning observations, and children’s anti-bullying behavior observation sheets. Quantitative data were analyzed using Aiken’s V, descriptive statistics, MSI transformation, normality testing, paired-sample t-test, and N-Gain. Results. The validation results showed that the model, instruments, and digital products were feasible to highly feasible, with Aiken’s V values ranging from 0.78 to 0.97. Children’s anti-bullying behavior scores increased from 26.13 in the pretest to 46.05 in the posttest, with a mean N-Gain of 0.367 in the moderate category. The paired-sample t-test showed a significant difference between pretest and posttest scores, t(94) = 25.38, p < 0.001. Teacher responses indicated that the model was practical, with an average practicality score of 81.25%. Conclusion. The developed model provides a feasible, practical, and initially effective approach to strengthening anti-bullying behavior in early childhood education through SEL-based interactive digital narrative learning. Further large-scale trials are needed to examine its broader effectiveness and adaptability.

title: Elevating Doctor of Nursing Practice impact: A collaborative framework for advancing nursing's practice doctorate.
abstract: Despite national guidance, Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) programs vary in project terminology, acceptable project types, faculty preparation, review processes, and evaluation and dissemination of practice change. Although some variation reflects local context, unclear distinctions among research, evidence-based practice, quality improvement, program evaluation, and policy analysis may hinder consistent preparation and communication of DNP scholarship. This article describes the formation, evolution, structure, and emerging work of the Texas DNP Directors Collaborative and presents its core components as a transferable framework for project excellence, academic-practice engagement, and practice scholarship. This descriptive account examines a voluntary statewide collaborative of DNP program leaders meeting quarterly for 14 years. Activities include rotating leadership, faculty development, peer consultation, and resource sharing. Early process indicators are described. Leaders from more than half of AACN-accredited DNP programs in Texas participate. Seven programs reported adopting the same model to guide DNP projects and curriculum. Other developments include shared faculty-development resources, discussions of project types and review processes, and student and practice-partner representation. Effects on project quality, partnerships, and practice outcomes have not been systematically evaluated. A sustained statewide collaborative offers a feasible structure for cross-program faculty development, academic-practice dialogue, and clarification of DNP project expectations. The framework may be adapted elsewhere, but its effects on educational, organizational, and practice outcomes require systematic evaluation.

title: Empowering Practice: An LPAA Aligned Mentoring Model for Professionals.
abstract: The life participation approach to aphasia (LPAA) is a model for prioritizing the reintegration of people with aphasia into meaningful life activities. Despite the importance of this model, challenges remain in teaching speech-language pathologists to implement it. In 2023, the Aphasia Access Membership Committee established the Life Participation Mentorship Program (LPM Program). The program provides structured one-on-one and group mentorship to a cohort of Aphasia Access members annually, with a focus on how LPAA integrates into clinical, research, and program development roles. We assessed the feasibility and acceptability of the LPM Program through online survey feedback provided by participants across three cohorts. Lessons learned were derived from survey feedback and Membership Committee reflection. The findings of the current study suggest that through individual guidance, resource sharing, and discussion of real-world challenges, the mentorship program may help mentees operationalize LPAA principles within diverse clinical, research, and organizational contexts. The LPM Program is part of a comprehensive organizational investment in future growth and sustainability of the LPAA model. Initiatives such as the LPM Program may help strengthen member engagement, expand organizational reach, and support the continued advancement of life participation-focused services.

title: Measuring moral motivation – a confirmatory factor analysis in a German sample of adolescents
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the factorial structure of a questionnaire assessing moral motivation within pictorial moral conflict stories in adolescents, based on theoretical moral motivation models. The questionnaire was assessed with N = 461 adolescents (n = 253 female, 54.88%; n = 208 male, 45.12%) with a mean age of 14.26 years (SD = 1.79, range = 10–19 years). The instrument consists of pictorial moral conflicts, depicting hypothetical conflicts in which participants evaluate moral decisions made by others and themselves, attribute emotions to moral and immoral actions, assess their sense of duty for moral actions, and judge the admissibility of immoral actions. The scenarios in the stories systematically vary in action orientation (prohibitive vs. prosocial), type of harm (physical, social, or property-related), and group affiliation (in-group vs. out-group). Confirmatory factor analysis showed that a model including only the six correlated dimensions did not adequately represent the data. Model fit improved substantially when orthogonal scenario factors were included to account for dependencies between responses referring to the same pictorial story. Overall, the findings support a multidimensional assessment of moral motivation while highlighting the importance of accounting for scenario-specific dependencies when using pictorial moral conflicts. This study provides a tool for assessing moral motivation in adolescents, offering new insights into the interplay between cognitive, emotional, and situational factors in moral conflicts.

title: Prosocial punishment bots breed social punishment in human players
abstract: Prosocial punishment, an important factor to stabilize cooperation in social dilemma games, often faces challenges like second-order free-riders-who cooperate but avoid punishing to save costs-and antisocial punishers, who defect and retaliate against cooperators. Addressing these challenges, our study introduces prosocial punishment bots that consistently cooperate and punish free-riders. Our findings reveal that these bots significantly promote the emergence of prosocial punishment among normal players due to their 'sticky effect'-an unwavering commitment to cooperation and punishment that magnetically attracts their opponents to emulate this strategy. Additionally, we observe that the prevalence of prosocial punishment is greatly enhanced when normal players exhibit a tendency to follow a 'copying the majority' strategy, or when bots are strategically placed in high-degree nodes within scale-free networks. Conversely, bots designed for defection or antisocial punishment diminish overall cooperation levels. This stark contrast underscores the critical role of strategic bot design in enhancing cooperative behaviours in human/AI interactions. Our findings open new avenues in evolutionary game theory, demonstrating the potential of human-machine collaboration in solving the conundrum of punishment.

title: Establishing Restorative Pedagogy Within Medical School Curriculum: Iterative Development of Shame and Resilience Discussion Utilizing Restorative Practices.
abstract: Student isolation and negative experiences of power dynamics, including shame, are well-documented contributors to student burnout. Traditional medical education lacks structured processes to promote resilience and minimize isolation. There is a need for intentional dialogue spaces to facilitate interpersonal connections and support. Restorative practices (RPs), such as community-building circles, represent potential tools to address these issues. However, there is no documented evidence of the use of RPs in medical school curricula. The authors adapted an existing discussion session on shame and resilience in the first-semester medical school curriculum by incorporating RP community-building circles. At the end of the session, individuals identified resilience strategies to address negative feelings. These structured conversations, led by trained facilitators, aimed to create equitable discussion environments. The approach focused on storytelling, minimizing power dynamics, and fostering a supportive learning environment. Student and facilitator perspectives were collected through anonymous surveys. Of the 177 students and 78 facilitators who participated, 172 students (97%) and 29 facilitators (37%) completed the anonymous surveys. Survey responses indicated a positive impact on student engagement, feelings of support, and equitable participation. Both students and facilitators found the circling method effective for sharing personal stories and promoting mutual support. They highlighted increased feelings of connection and comfort with vulnerability. However, some perceived structural limitations and discomfort with vulnerability were noted. Future work should focus on the long-term evaluation of learners' perceptions of RPs, the intervention's impact on resilience, and students' continued use of identified resilience strategies. In addition, longitudinal incorporation of RPs across the curriculum is recommended.

title: Technology transfer and industrial relocation in Shanghai's biomedical industry: challenges and policy implications.
abstract: The biomedical industry is one of three priority industries for development in Shanghai. However, the contradiction of 'conducting research and development (R&D) in Shanghai, while technology transfer flows elsewhere' is increasingly apparent. Although Shanghai has a high concentration of R&D institutions, innovative talent, and capital, much of its R&D is industrialized in the surrounding Yangtze River Delta and beyond. This structural separation brings potential public-health risks, including supply-chain fragility and inequity of medical product access. This paper analyzes the causes of this relocation from a Shanghai perspective, qualitatively assesses its potential consequences for Shanghai's economy, public finances, national innovation ecosystem and public health, and proposes countermeasures. Industrial relocation enables Shanghai to upgrade its industrial structure and clarify its positioning as an innovation-driven city. Although the relocation of industrialization activities has a certain degree of structural inevitability, its effects are conditional. The specific outcomes depend on which segments are relocated, the relationships of ownership and control, knowledge-feedback mechanisms, industrial supporting capacity, and cross-regional benefit-sharing arrangements. Unmanaged separation of R&D and manufacturing may threaten medical supply-chain resilience. Shanghai's biomedical industry is characterized by R&D agglomeration and industrial relocation, a structural feature shaped by cost, policy, and ecosystem factors, calling for regional collaborative governance to mitigate both economic and public-health risks.

title: Development and Evaluation of Embeddings for Representing Injuries in Patients With Traumatic Injuries: Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Patients with traumatic injuries present with heterogeneous injury patterns that are difficult to represent in statistical models. Common approaches either retain individual injury codes in high-dimensional sparse representations, such as one-hot encoding, or aggregate injuries into summary scores, reducing dimensionality at the cost of patient-specific detail. This study aimed to develop low-dimensional data-driven ICD-10 embeddings for traumatic injuries and compare their downstream discriminatory performance with one-hot encoding of the same injury codes. We conducted a retrospective study using National Trauma Data Bank (NTDB) records from 2018 and 2019. International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification diagnoses were mapped to World Health Organization ICD-10 codes, retaining traumatic-injury codes S00-S99 and T15-T34. A denoising autoencoder was developed on 2018 data and temporally evaluated on 2019 data. Representations with 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64 dimensions were compared with one-hot encoding across 16 downstream tasks using logistic regression and LightGBM. Performance was measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for binary tasks and macro one-vs-rest AUC for multiclass tasks. Models were trained and evaluated within individual hospitals and separately on the full NTDB. Hospitals were stratified into volume categories, from small (≤500) to major (2500 patients/year). CIs were obtained from 1000 nonparametric bootstrap samples. The development cohort included 1,041,021 eligible patients from 2018, and the temporal evaluation cohort included 1,094,933 patients from 2019. At the hospital level, embeddings outperformed one-hot encoding. With LightGBM at 16 dimensions, the mean paired AUC difference across tasks was 0.054 (95% CI 0.048-0.060) in small hospitals (n=120) vs 0.023 (95% CI 0.020-0.025) in major hospitals (n=99). With logistic regression, differences were 0.056 (95% CI 0.050-0.063) and 0.041 (95% CI 0.039-0.043), respectively. In the full NTDB, 803-indicator one-hot encoding outperformed embeddings. Mean differences were -0.004 (95% CI -0.004 to -0.003) with LightGBM and -0.030 (95% CI -0.030 to -0.029) with logistic regression. At 64 dimensions, these differences narrowed to -0.001 and -0.016, respectively. Embeddings with as few as 8 dimensions achieved predictive performance comparable to or better than one-hot encoding, with up to a 100-fold reduction in dimensionality. Compared to one-hot encoding, embeddings improved performance in models trained at individual hospitals, particularly lower-volume hospitals. These gains may reflect reduced dimensionality, parameter sharing across codes, and representation of codes absent from hospital-specific training data, enabled by embeddings learned from the larger development cohort. In models trained on the full registry, one-hot encoding achieved higher mean AUC with both estimators, although the differences were minor (<0.005 AUC difference) for LightGBM with 16- to 64-dimensional embeddings. The embeddings and software are openly available.

title: Interpersonal Attraction and Prosocial Behavior in College Students: Unveiling the Nexus
abstract: This research is based on the problems experienced by students of Muhammadiyah Sidoarjo University, namely the indication of a lack of prosocial behavior. It can be seen from the results of interviews that there is a lack of cooperation, honesty and help between students. Researchers are interested in examining the relationship between interpersonal attraction and prosocial behavior in Muhammadiyah Sidoarjo University students. Based on the above problems, this study aims to determine the relationship between interpersonal attraction and prosocial behavior of Muhammadiyah Sidoarjo University students. The research model applied is correlational research using a quantitative approach. This research uses quantitative methods of correlational quantitative methods. Variables in the study “The Relationship Between Interpersonal Attraction With Prosocial Behavior In Students of Muhammadiyah University of Sidoarjo” include The independent variable used in this study is Interpersonal Attraction. The dependent variable used in this study is Prosocial Behavior. Based on the results of the analysis, the results of the research data analysis test obtained show a correlation coefficient value of 0.997 with a significance of 0.000 < 0.05. This means that there is a significant relationship between interpersonal attraction and prosocial behavior. Based on the results of the coefficient of determination test, the results show 0.735 (R-Square), which means that in this study the Interpersonal Attraction variable makes an effective contribution of 73.5% to the prosocial behavior variable. Based on the results of the research that has been carried out, the hypothesis proposed is accepted with a positive correlation between Interpersonal Attraction and Prosocial Behavior in Muhammadiyah Sidoarjo University Students. According to the results of hypothesis testing above, it can be seen that the Interpersonal Attraction and Prosocial Behavior data are normally distributed and have a linear relationship. The results of hypothesis testing using Pearson correlation show a correlation coefficient of 0.997 significance 0.000 < 0.05.

title: Positive death attitudes and psychological well-being: examining the influence of the four immeasurables.
abstract: The global ageing population trend has heightened the need to understand various factors affecting geriatric well-being, including beliefs and attitudes about death. Positive perspectives about death, such as those gained from practicing maranasati (death contemplation in Buddhism), may enhance psychological resilience and prosocial behavior, key factors promoted in public mental health. Death reflection can encourage the development of the Four Immeasurable Minds (equanimity, loving-kindness, compassion, and sympathetic joy), Buddhist virtues that promote public harmony and enhance well-being. The current study investigated whether positive beliefs and attitudes about death influenced well-being directly or indirectly through the Four Immeasurable Minds among older Thai Buddhists, contributing to culturally informed mental health strategies. Data were collected from 332 older adults in Northern Thailand. The study collected information on positive beliefs and attitudes about death using the Morana Questionnaire, well-being using the WHO-5 index (Thai), and Four Immeasurable Minds using the Four Immeasurable Inventory. The data were analyzed using mediation analysis, accounting for potential confounding variables. Positive beliefs about death had a significant and positive effect on well-being, and prosocial values mediated this relationship. The findings suggest that positive beliefs about death can promote prosocial values and contribute to a healthy sense of well-being among Buddhist Thai older adult. Integrating culturally adapted, mindfulness-based approaches into public mental health initiatives could support healthy aging, particularly in Buddhist communities. Further research should explore scalable interventions to promote psychological resilience in diverse older populations.

title: Sustainable Altruism: Simulating the Future of Prosociality and Peacebuilding—A Conceptual Review
abstract: In this article, we argue for the potential value of participatory multi-agent artificial intelligence (MAAI) modeling for addressing the pragmatic challenge of promoting a sustainable altruism among individuals and groups that will enable us to find pathways of collective action that lead toward more peaceful coexistence. Along the way, we note that this approach to modeling also addresses the scientific challenge within computer science and social simulation of creating more psychologically realistic artificial agents whose interactions occur in more realistic social networks. We identify some of the evolved cognitive and coalitional biases that make it so difficult to achieve an equilibrium of sustainable altruism in contemporary human societies, describe some of the innovative ways in which recent advances in MAAI approaches to psychological and cultural modeling open up new opportunities for simulating solutions to these challenges, and address some of the ethical issues associated with using modeling and simulating methods to help us proactively navigate the Anthropocene.

title: Delineating Empathy and Sympathy: A Comparative Bibliometric Analysis and an Operational Indicator Framework (2015-2025)
abstract: Empathy and sympathy have been widely recognized as core antecedents of prosocial behavior. However, prior literature has treated the two constructs inconsistently, with sympathy frequently subsumed under an overly broad and ill - defined conceptualization of empathy. This conceptual overlap has limited discriminant operationalization, hindered cumulative theoretical development, and consequently constrained applied precision in interdisciplinary contexts. The present study examined whether empathy and sympathy constituted structurally distinguishable knowledge domains with divergent intellectual foundations and developmental trajectories. A comparative bibliometric analysis was conducted using SSCI-indexed articles retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection for the period 2015-2025. The dataset comprised 4,413 empathy-related publications and 247 sympathy-related publications. VOSviewer and CiteSpace were employed to perform keyword co-occurrence mapping, document co-citation clustering, burst detection, and strategic coordinate analysis. This study provided the first comparative scientometric evidence to distinguish the structural divergence between empathy and sympathy research. Results showed that empathy research formed a dense, interdisciplinary, and mature thematic structure, whereas sympathy research was relatively small, fragmented, and often subsumed under empathy-related clusters. Based on quantitative mapping and theoretical integration, we developed a four-dimensional operational indicator framework with fifteen second-order indicators. This framework translates structural knowledge patterns into a systematic conceptual reference for future measurement and modeling studies. By combining scientometric analysis with conceptual reconstruction, this study helps clarify a long-standing definitional ambiguity and provides a novel data-driven approach for differentiating overlapping constructs in social science research.

title: The expression of self-conscious emotions and their motivational and communicative function in early development
abstract: Self-conscious emotions, such as embarrassment, guilt, shame and pride, play a central role in managing reputation and interpersonal relationships. They are thought to emerge in the first years of life, with children's developing cognitive capacities and their growing appreciation of social norms and rules. Recent years have seen a rapid increase in research on self-conscious emotions in early life, supported by advanced methods including manual and automated micro-coding of non-verbal behaviour, depth sensor imaging and physiological measures. In this narrative review, we summarize this emerging evidence from developmental science, which suggests that self-conscious emotions may be observed earlier than previously thought-within the first months and years of life-and that they seem to serve both motivational and communicative functions from early on. Specifically, they motivate socially appropriate behaviours, such as helping others, while communicating adherence to social norms and rules. Further, we highlight current limitations in the field and recommend more experimental and longitudinal studies especially in infancy and toddlerhood, the integration of multi-modal data and the use of naturalistic tasks to advance our understanding of self-conscious emotions in early development. This article is part of the theme issue 'Mechanisms, development, phylogeny and functions of emotional expressions'.

title: The Life-sustenance Hypothesis: Understanding Human-Nature Connection by Integrating Rousseau's Philosophy to Contemporary Systems Biological Viewpoints
abstract: This paper develops the life-sustenance hypothesis to explain the multifaceted phenomenon of the human-nature connection. It is based on an interpretation of Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy brought into contemporary times via recent multidisciplinary research and theoretical underpinnings. Rousseau suggested that humans have two innate, instinctive drives he called amour-de-soi and pitié—a self-preservative drive, and its enlargement, an inclination to help other living beings in distress. The life-sustenance hypothesis is rooted in a systems biological framework situating humans as interconnected parts within a nested system of life. Corresponding to Rousseau’s drives, this interconnectedness is suggested to give rise to the dynamics between two life-preserving orientations that guide our manners-of-being in the world: a self-sustaining and a ‘life-sustaining’ orientation shared by all organisms, albeit manifested differently. The experience of nature connectedness, along with altruistic impulses, are proposed to be human manifestations of the life-sustaining orientation. Moreover, in line with Rousseau’s philosophy, it is posited that the modern, individualistic lifestyle has given rise to an imbalance between these orientations leading to problems in prosociality, proenvironmentalism, and overall well-being. One means by which to regain balanced manners-of-being might be to enhance our nature connectedness. Possible physiological indicators for the hypothesis are explored.

title: How to define and promote flourishing in children in the context of early childhood education and care
abstract: This scoping review maps key constructs of child flourishing, examines their conceptualization and measurement, and synthesizes their associations with developmental outcomes. A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were screened using predefined criteria, focusing on individual-level positive psychological resources (e.g., subjective wellbeing, gratitude, hope, character strengths, resilience, and self-efficacy) and children's experiences within the Early Childhood Education and Care (ECEC) context with positive education. In total, 68 studies were included in the final review. Data were charted and synthesized narratively. Evidence suggests that these constructs demonstrate generally stable development across early childhood and are associated with positive outcomes, including social-emotional competence, prosocial behavior, and learning engagement. Partial support was found for the broaden-and-built theory and the undoing hypothesis. Measurement approaches varied considerably across studies, with a lack of consistent, standardized instruments and limited evidence on the developmental trajectories of these constructs. Children's experiences in ECEC, particularly character education through art, resilience projects through teamwork and mindfulness, emerged as integral to flourishing and interacted with psychological resources. Greater conceptual clarity, standardized measures, and inclusive, theory-driven research are needed to advance the field.

title: Protocol for an agent-based model of recombination in bacteria playing a public goods game.
abstract: Agent-based models are composed of individual agents coded for traits, such as cooperation and cheating, that interact in a virtual world based on defined rules. Here, we describe the use of an agent-based model of homologous recombination in bacteria playing a public goods game. We describe steps for software installation, setting model parameters, running and testing models, and visualization and statistical analysis. This protocol is useful in analyses of horizontal gene transfer, bacterial sociobiology, and game theory. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Lee et al.

title: Resolving social dilemmas with minimal reward transfer
abstract: Social dilemmas present a significant challenge in multi-agent cooperation because individuals are incentivised to behave in ways that undermine socially optimal outcomes. Consequently, self-interested agents often avoid collective behaviour. In response, we formalise social dilemmas and introduce a novel metric, the general self-interest level, to quantify the disparity between individual and group rationality in such scenarios. This metric represents the maximum proportion of their individual rewards that agents can retain while ensuring that a social welfare optimum becomes a dominant strategy. Our approach diverges from traditional concepts of altruism, instead focusing on strategic reward redistribution. By transferring rewards among agents in a manner that aligns individual and group incentives, rational agents will maximise collective welfare while pursuing their own interests. We provide an algorithm to compute efficient transfer structures for an arbitrary number of agents, and introduce novel multi-player social dilemma games to illustrate the effectiveness of our method. This work provides both a descriptive tool for analysing social dilemmas and a prescriptive solution for resolving them via efficient reward transfer contracts. Applications include mechanism design, where we can assess the impact on collaborative behaviour of modifications to models of environments.

title: Evaluations of aggressive chasing interactions by 7‐month‐old infants
abstract: Recent theories of socio-moral development assume that humans evolved a capacity to evaluate others' social actions in different kinds of interactions. Prior infant studies found both reaching and visual preferences for the prosocial over the antisocial agents. However, whether the attribution of either positive or negative valence to agents' actions involved in an aggressive chasing interaction can be inferred by both reaching behaviors and visual attention deployment (i.e., disengagement of visual attention) is still an open question. Here we presented 7-month-old infants (N = 92) with events displaying an aggressive chasing interaction. By using preferential reaching and an attentional task (i.e., overlap paradigm), we assessed whether and how infants evaluate aggressive chasing interactions. The results demonstrated that young infants prefer to reach the victim over the aggressor, but neither agent affects visual attention. Moreover, such reaching preferences emerged only when dynamic cues and emotional face-like features were congruent with agents' social roles. Overall, these findings suggested that infants' evaluations of aggressive interactions are based on infants' sensitivity to some kinematic cues that characterized agents' actions and, especially, to the congruency between such motions and the face-like emotional expressions of the agents.

title: Examining the impact of attentional focus and partner gaze on interpersonal coordination.
abstract: As a foundation of social interaction, interpersonal coordination is boosted in prosocial contexts but undermined by negative situations. Exactly how social factors shape coordination is, however, unknown. Previous literature demonstrates that for coordination to emerge people must attend to their interaction partners. This evidence, however, draws from sterile laboratory studies employing heavy-handed manipulations of little interpersonal relevance. By contrast, in more naturalistic contexts subtle differences in how people attend to themselves and others (e.g., a lingering glance vs. a suspicious side glance) can profoundly change the course of interaction. Understanding how social factors shape interpersonal coordination therefore requires consideration of aspects of attentional behaviour that better characterise everyday interaction. To this end, the current research employed virtual reality (VR) to explore how two core features of social attention, focus (self vs. other) and partner gaze (direct vs. averted), influence the spontaneous coordination of arm and head movements. The results indicated that: (i) coordination was enhanced in the other (cf. self) focus condition; and (ii) coordination was diminished in the averted (cf. direct) gaze condition. These findings provide novel evidence to indicate that the emergence of interpersonal coordination varies as a function of the everyday attentional behaviours that punctuate naturalistic social exchange. Of broad theoretical note, here we demonstrate that the among the factors constraining interpersonal coordination, the distribution of attention between self and other plays a meaningful role.

title: Impact of pig farming activities on the gut microbiome and resistome of farmers: insights from metagenomics and Escherichia coli genomics.
abstract: Intensive swine production entails high antimicrobial use and close human-animal microbial exchange, with potential to remodel the human gut ecosystem and promote cross-host antimicrobial resistance (AMR) transmission. To quantify the impact of occupational exposure on the human gut microbiome and resistome, and to resolve putative livestock-to-human gene flow, we sampled feces from 103 swine farms in Sichuan, China. We generated metagenomes for 431 samples (farmers = 96, residents = 97, pigs = 238) and cultured 833 Escherichia coli isolates (farmers = 80, residents = 88, pigs = 665). Relative to unexposed residents, farmers exhibited reduced gut α-diversity and lower Gut Microbiome Health Index (GMHI). Taxonomic and functional profiles differed between farmers and residents, with farmers showing reduced abundances of several fiber-degrading and short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa, together with increased abundances of taxa and pathways related to mucin-derived glycan utilization. The resistome displayed an exposure gradient (pigs > farmers > residents). Farmers were enriched for determinants corresponding to commonly used veterinary drug classes (e.g., florfenicol, quinolones, MLS, aminoglycosides), whereas β-lactam genes were proportionally lower. Mobile genetic element (MGE) analysis revealed a pig-centered plasmid reservoir: among 157,298 nonredundant plasmid contigs, 1,415 carried ARGs, with 83.1%/18.3%/3.9% enriched in pigs/farmers/residents; notably, 88.8% of farmer-enriched plasmid contigs were co-enriched in pigs and harbored clinically important genes such as optrA, cfr, and mcr-10.1. ARG-bearing phages were rare (106/227,476) but predominantly pig-associated. E. coli genomics indicated limited cross-host clonal transmission (five pig-farmer and one pig-resident events) yet higher ARG burdens in pig and farmer isolates. A random-forest classifier based on metagenomic taxonomic profiles distinguished farmers from residents (AUC = 0.921; specificity = 0.9; sensitivity = 0.775), nominating Schaalia odontolytica and Acinetobacter lwoffii as candidate exposure biomarkers. This study characterized the gut microbiome and resistome of pig-farm workers, non-farming residents, and pigs, revealing an association between occupational exposure to swine production and alterations in the gut microbiome and resistome of farmers. Shared ARG and plasmid-associated features suggest that MGEs may contribute to resistome overlap at the livestock-human interface, although the mechanisms of exchange require validation through longitudinal, environment-integrated, and strain-resolved studies. Overall, these results provide a basis for future One Health investigations of microbial and ARG sharing at the livestock-human interface. Video Abstract.

title: Drama temelli hikâye anlatıcılığıyla orman okullarındaki okul öncesi öğrencilerinin dinleme ve empati becerilerinin geliştirilmesi
abstract: Bu çalışma, doğadan ilham alan bir öğrenme bağlamında, drama temelli hikâye anlatımının okul öncesi öğrencilerinde dinleme becerileri ve empati farkındalıkları üzerindeki etkisini incelemektedir. Empati kavramı, mevcut literatür kapsamında sosyo-duygusal gelişimin önemli bir yönü olarak kabul edilmektedir. Bu önemin farkında olarak; yaratıcı ve sanat temelli pedagojik yöntemler çerçevesinde yürütülen bu araştırma ile empati olgusunun erken dil eğitimine etkileri noktasında literatürde duyulan sistematik yaklaşım ihtiyacının giderilmesi için çalışılmıştır. Bu doğrultuda yürütülen çalışmada 5-6 yaş arası 32 çocukla yarı deneysel, karma metod araştırma tasarımı kullanılmıştır. Özenle tasarlanmış dört hikâye sekiz hafta boyunca işlenmiş; iki hikâye, doğa temasıyla zenginleştirilmiş bir sınıfta, iki hikâye ise okulun bahçesinde, ön-son çerçeve ve drama etkinlikleri kullanılarak gerçekleştirilmiştir. Nicel veriler, araştırmacının çalışma için tasarladığı dinleme başarı testi ve geçerliliği kanıtlanmış olan Çocuklar için Empati Ölçeği (ÇEMÖ) kullanılarak toplanmıştır. Eşleştirilmiş örneklem t-testi bulguları, dinleme becerilerinde ise istatistiksel olarak anlamlı gelişmeler olduğunun ve empati farkındalığının arttığı sonucuna ulaşılmıştır. İlgili nitel bulgular, okul öncesi katılımcıların dikkat sürelerinin, duygusal kelime dağarcıklarının ve prososyal davranışlarının da arttığını göstermiştir. Açık hava öğrenme ortamı, öğrenme faaliyetlerine yönelik daha duyusal bir deneyimi destekleyebilirken, sınıflar buna göre uyarlandığında, içeride de benzer niteliksel ve niceliksel sonuçlar kaydedilmiştir. Araştırma kapsamında elde edilen bulgular; sosyokültürel, gelişimsel ve deneyimsel öğrenme çerçeveleri tarafından yönlendirilen drama ile zenginleştirilmiş hikâye anlatımının, erken yaştaki İngilizce öğrenen çocuklar için kapsamlı bir pedagojik yaklaşım sağlayarak dil eğitiminin sosyo-duygusal gelişimle başarılı bir şekilde birleştirebileceğini ortaya çıkarmıştır.

title: Interprofessional collaboration as a mediator between empathy and lifelong learning in health professions education: a multigroup structural equation modeling approach.
abstract: Professionalism in health professions education is increasingly understood as a multidimensional construct integrating empathy, interprofessional collaboration, and lifelong learning. While each dimension has been linked to positive educational outcomes, their structural interrelationships and potential disciplinary differences remain insufficiently examined. This study aims to investigate the interrelationships among empathy, physician-nurse collaboration, and lifelong learning across medical and nursing disciplines. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among undergraduate medical and nursing students from four Peruvian universities (N = 1,707). Empathy, physician-nurse collaboration, and lifelong learning were measured using validated Jefferson Scales. Propensity score matching produced two demographically balanced groups (600 medical, 600 nursing students). Group differences were examined using t tests. Mediation analyses with bias-corrected bootstrapping were conducted separately by discipline. Multigroup structural equation modeling tested cross-disciplinary invariance. Nursing students scored significantly higher in collaboration (Cohen's d = 1.24) and lifelong learning (Cohen's d = 0.45) than medical students. In both groups, empathy was positively associated with lifelong learning through the mediating role of collaboration. Notably, the indirect effect was significantly stronger in nursing students (58.18% of total effect) than in medical students (34.48%). Multigroup comparison confirmed that this disciplinary difference was driven by the stronger impact of collaboration on lifelong learning in the nursing cohort (Δχ Physician-nurse collaboration partially mediates the relationship between empathy and lifelong learning, with a substantially stronger effect in nursing students. These findings highlight interprofessional collaboration as a critical social-learning pathway for transforming empathic dispositions into sustained professional development.

title: Modified Cardiometabolic Index and Incident Surrogate-Defined Cardiovascular-Liver-Metabolic Multimorbidity Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults in China: A Prospective Cohort Study from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).
abstract: Defined by the coexistence of at least two cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes and suspected metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, cardiovascular-liver-metabolic multimorbidity (CLMM) is an emerging phenotype that is related to the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic continuum yet distinct from it. By combining triglycerides, fasting glucose, HDL cholesterol and central adiposity, the modified cardiometabolic index (MCMI) summarizes these features in a single fasting-panel measure. Evidence to date has been confined to cross-sectional fatty-liver and self-reported outcomes; established lipid-glucose indices have not been compared head to head with MCMI for CLMM. We included 6124 CHARLS participants aged 45 years or older, free of CLMM in 2011 and with a 2015 health questionnaire. For the primary analysis, we assigned indeterminate follow-up outcomes ( Over approximately four years, 619 participants (10.11%) fulfilled the surrogate-defined CLMM definition, with suspected MASLD documented in 93.4% of cases. A nonlinear association was observed ( MCMI was associated with incident surrogate-defined CLMM, yet much of the observed association appeared attributable to pre-existing component burden and to the LAP-based suspected MASLD component sharing inputs with MCMI, while its magnitude varied with the treatment of indeterminate outcomes. Its exploratory apparent discrimination was not significantly different from that of BMI or waist-to-height ratio. Interpretation remains limited by the lack of independent validation; the joint MCMI-CRP findings did not establish interaction or biological synergy.

title: Designing Social Minds : How AI Design and Communication Norms Shape Human Perception, Engagement, and Prosocial Behavior
abstract: Concevoir des esprits sociaux : Comment le design de l'IA et les normes de communication façonnent la perception, l'engagement et le comportement prosocial des humains L'importance des agents conversationnels numériques a récemment augmenté, de nombreuses entreprises adoptant des agents pilotés par l'IA pour gérer les demandes d'affaires et faciliter les interactions quotidiennes avec les clients. Étant donné la réticence générale des individus envers l'IA, certaines entreprises choisissent d'anthropomorphiser leurs bots de service client (par exemple, en leur donnant des noms et des avatars). Cependant, l'efficacité de ces pratiques n'est pas claire dans le cas des voicebots (c'est-à-dire, des bots conversationnels basés sur la voix), car ces interventions ne sont pas axées sur la voix. Nous nous concentrons sur la voix, en tant que caractéristique clé des voicebots, et proposons une approche d'anthropomorphisme axée sur la voix. À travers une série de cinq expériences, nous démontrons le rôle de l'attribution d'un accent au voicebot sur les perceptions anthropomorphiques et l'engagement ultérieur des utilisateurs. Plus précisément, nous montrons que les utilisateurs ont une préférence plus marquée pour interagir avec des voicebots et adoptent des attitudes plus positives envers eux lorsque ces voicebots sont équipés d'accents étrangers. Nous mettons en lumière le rôle sous-jacent des perceptions anthropomorphiques en tant que mécanisme psychologique, suggérant que les accents étrangers servent de cue anthropomorphique crucial, influençant l'attitude des utilisateurs et entraînant une préférence pour les voicebots par rapport aux agents en direct. Ces résultats fournissent des éclairages pour les entreprises cherchant à améliorer l'engagement client grâce à leur voicebot, ainsi que pour les entreprises impliquées dans le développement des technologies voicebot

title: Differential inflammation by Salmonella serovars is independent of FliC inflammasome activation.
abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium and Salmonella Choleraesuis display distinct clinical manifestations, yet the molecular basis for their differential inflammatory potential, particularly via outer membrane vesicles (OMV), are not fully understood. Here, we examined the role of FliC in the differential inflammatory responses induced by S. Typhimurium UK-1 and S. Choleraesuis C78-3 and their corresponding OMV. In vivo, UK-1 infection triggered significantly elevated serum levels of IL-1β and IL-6 compared with C78-3 infection, a difference that was also observed following OMV administration. Isogenic fliC deletion mutants, which lacked both flagella and OMV-associated flagellin, were successfully generated. While wild-type bacteria and their OMV robustly activated the NLRC4 inflammasome pathway in bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), resulting in caspase-1 cleavage and IL-1β maturation, the ΔfliC mutants and their OMV exhibited markedly diminished activity. Notably, recombinant FliC proteins from the two serovars, despite sharing only 77% amino acid homology, activated the inflammasome with comparable efficiency. A key finding was that UK-1(ΔfliC) and its OMV still induced higher IL-1β production than C78-3(ΔfliC) counterparts both in vitro and in vivo, indicating that the enhanced immunostimulatory capacity of UK-1 is mediated by factors independent of FliC. Collectively, this study provides new insights into the serovar-specific inflammatory mechanisms of Salmonella and suggests that FliC-independent factors warrant consideration in the development of OMV-based vaccines and the understanding of inflammatory responses.

title: Transformative health justice framework for conducting translational antiracism research.
abstract: Structural racism remains a key driver of persistent health inequities in the United States, yet translating institutional commitments to equity into actionable strategies remains a challenge for many health systems. While existing implementation frameworks offer valuable tools, few provide integrated, community-informed approaches for designing structural interventions that can function across multiple levels of care. The Transformative Health Justice Framework (THJF) was developed to meet this need. It draws from systems science, behavioral intervention development, and community-engaged research, combining three established models, the ORBIT model, the National Academy of Medicine's community engagement benchmarks, and the Social Ecological Model of Racism and Antiracism, into a coherent, phased process. We applied the THJF within two integrated primary care systems in a Southeastern state to support the design of interventions co-led by local stakeholders. By embedding equity principles into measurable planning activities, such as power-sharing agreements, lived experience integration, and structural accountability mechanisms. This paper demonstrates how structural change can be systematically organized, even in politically constrained and under-resourced settings. The framework's adaptability positions it as a timely contribution to the evolving public health landscape, where equity work must remain both rigorous and responsive to shifting social and cultural conditions.

title: Integrated Pan-Cancer Profiling of the Human Lysine Deacetylase Superfamily Identifies SIRT7 as a Central Regulator of Genome Stability and Cancer Progression.
abstract: Lysine deacetylases (KDACs) are central regulators of chromatin organization, transcription, metabolism, DNA repair, and cellular signaling, yet their molecular and clinical landscape across human cancers has not been systematically defined. Here, we performed the first comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of the complete human lysine deacetylase superfamily by integrating transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical datasets across The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Systematic analyses of all 18 human deacetylases revealed extensive but highly heterogeneous patterns of dysregulation, demonstrating that individual family members exhibit distinct transcriptional profiles, copy-number alterations, mutation frequencies, and prognostic associations despite sharing a common catalytic function. HDAC10 and SIRT6 emerged as the most consistently overexpressed deacetylases, whereas SIRT1 and HDAC4 displayed widespread transcriptional repression. Copy-number analysis identified SIRT7 as the most frequently amplified deacetylase across human malignancies, while survival analysis further demonstrated that elevated SIRT7 expression was associated with adverse clinical outcomes, particularly in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma. Integrative multi-omics prioritization identified SIRT7 as the highest-confidence candidate for mechanistic investigation. Integration of human SIRT7 knockout transcriptomic datasets with TCGA-derived expression profiles identified 204 conserved SIRT7-activated genes and 135 conserved SIRT7-repressed genes, which were significantly enriched for pathways governing cell-cycle progression, chromosome segregation, DNA replication, and genome maintenance. Network-based prioritization further identified PIF1, TROAP, AURKB, KIF18B, CHTF18, PKMYT1, MYBL2, and CDCA3 as central components of a conserved SIRT7-associated regulatory module. Collectively, this study establishes the first comprehensive pan-cancer molecular atlas of the human lysine deacetylase superfamily and demonstrates that deacetylases comprise a functionally diverse network of cancer regulators rather than a homogeneous class of epigenetic enzymes. Beyond prioritizing SIRT7 as a clinically relevant deacetylase linked to genome maintenance and mitotic progression, our integrative analytical framework provides a valuable resource for biomarker discovery, mechanistic investigation, and the development of precision epigenetic therapies.

title: Raising public awareness on radiation science.
abstract: The United Nations Scientific Committee on the Effects of Atomic Radiation (UNSCEAR) was established in 1955 by the United Nations General Assembly with the mandate to undertake broad assessments of the sources of ionising radiation and its effects on human health and the environment. In the past 68 years, the Committee has published 112 scientific annexes as reports to the General Assembly and five white articles. This article summarises the implementation of the Committee's public information and outreach strategy (2020-2024) in developing information material and new initiatives for raising public awareness on radiation effects and sharing knowledge and experiences with young professionals in order to foster the development of the next generation of radiation scientists.

title: [Development and application of Shenzhen Pathogen Genomic Big Data Surveillance and Early Warning System].
abstract: In the context of accelerating globalization and urbanization, emerging infectious diseases usually have more rapid spread and broader impact. Genomic surveillance can reveal the origins, mutations, transmission pathways, and drug resistance of pathogens, and has thus become a key technical tool for precise prevention and control of modern infectious diseases. As a megacity with "high population density, high population mobility and export-oriented characteristics", Shenzhen needs to have a precise prevention and control system that has integration with genomic data in the field of infectious disease pathogen surveillance. To improve infectious disease surveillance, early warning, and identification of unknown pathogens, Shenzhen Pathogen Genomic Big Data Surveillance and Early Warning System has been established by Shenzhen CDC to create a city-wide network for pathogen genomic data transmission and sharing for the early identification and dynamic tracking of infectious diseases and the precise prevention and control of infectious diseases.

title: Veterinary allergy diagnosis for a better pathophysiology-based treatment: A progressive story towards the future.
abstract: Allergy is a condition as old as human and animal life. In turn, allergy diagnosis is much more recent, evolving as quickly as medical and veterinary science since the 20 th century.Allergy diagnosis should follow well-established guidelines, aiming at a precise diagnosis by clinical and laboratory approaches. Clinical conditions were already being described when the discovery of immunoglobulin (Ig) E in 1967 allowed for a better understanding of the pathophysiology of significant allergic conditions like anaphylaxis, leading to the development of allergen immunotherapy. Then, as scientific knowledge progressed, the process of diagnosis also underwent the necessary adjustments, mirroring the advances in both allergen identification and pathophysiology. While a few decades ago, veterinary medicine mostly adapted the human allergology concepts as they were born, human and animal medicine currently move forward side by side, also in the field of immunoallergology. Sharing the same environmental conditions, humans and animals are both considered mutual models in allergy, whether regarding skin or respiratory conditions. Thanks to technology evolution, modern systems of complementary laboratory diagnosis are now available for molecular allergy diagnosis, allowing the so-called individual Component-resolved Diagnosis (CRD) and the subsequent more efficient Component-resolved Immunotherapy (CRIT) in the context of multimodal treatment, which science has shown to be the superior therapeutic approach. This manuscript focuses on this evolution, putting it in perspective.

title: From Bedside to National Conferences: Empowering Nurses Through a Clinical Nurse Mentor Program.
abstract: This article describes how the clinical nurse specialist empowered clinical nurses in disseminating scholarly work by developing a structured evidence-based clinical nurse mentor (CNM) program aimed at enhancing abstract writing skills, building confidence in presenting, and fostering professional growth. Presenting at conferences supports professional development by enabling nurses to share expertise, contribute to their profession, and advance their careers. Limited time, resources, lack of confidence, and leadership support are barriers to presenting. In 2022, the clinical nurse specialist identified the need for mentorship to empower nurses to share clinical expertise internally and externally. The Iowa model of "evidence-based practice" was utilized to guide implementation of the CNM program in the rehabilitation hospital. Over the 4-year period (fiscal year 23 to fiscal year26), 41 abstracts were submitted to local and national conferences, resulting in an 80% acceptance rate. Since program inception, 33 abstracts were submitted by 18 clinical nurses, 3 nursing supervisors, and 1 occupational therapist. Postimplementation, it was discovered that once nurses acquired these skills, they consistently submitted abstracts. The CNM Program enhanced and fostered a supportive and healthy work environment for clinical nurses, enabling professional development, leadership growth, and empowerment in sharing clinical expertise.

title: Development of Intervention Concepts for Reducing Intersectional Stigma in HIV Health Care Settings: Generated Concepts by Key Interest Holders Using Human-Centered Design.
abstract: Intersectional stigma is a robust barrier to HIV testing, linkage to care, and poorer adherence to HIV care and treatment; yet, few evidence-based interventions addressing intersectional stigma exist for health care settings. Community-centered approaches are critical to develop relevant, feasible, and impactful intervention opportunities. Human-centered design (HCD) offers a set of structured methods to center end users' experiences and needs to develop meaningful, community-proposed solutions. This two-phased project in Pennsylvania utilized iterative HCD methods (October 2022-October 2023) to identify challenges and opportunities for intersectional stigma reduction work in health care and co-design interventions for HIV care settings. Forty-one key interest holders, including people living with HIV and individuals working in HIV care settings, participated in the HCD activities of sharing, prioritizing, generating, and refining health care-based intervention concepts for reducing experiences of intersectional stigma for people living with HIV. Engagement activities resulted in eight co-created intervention concepts to support patient-centered, non-stigmatizing health care for all in HIV clinic spaces. Participants designed intervention concepts specific to clinical culture and environment, capacity building, and institutional and structural levels, with concepts reflective of the voices, lived experiences, and ideas of people living with HIV and those working in HIV care settings. Findings provide a foundational blueprint for integrating intersectional stigma reduction strategies to improve the health and well-being of people living with HIV.

title: H-Trp-Glu-OH and H-Glu-Trp-OH dipeptides as potential anticancer agents against glioblastoma multiforme: Multi-target molecular docking, DFT analysis, molecular dynamics simulation, ADMET profiling, and cell viability validation.
abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most common and lethal primary brain malignancy in adults. Despite the Stupp protocol, median overall survival remains approximately 15 months, and the inadequacy of current therapies combined with the restrictive permeability of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) underscore the need for new therapeutic candidates. This study aimed to evaluate the sequence isomeric dipeptides H-tryptophan-glutamic acid-OH (H-Trp-Glu-OH) and H-glutamic acid-tryptophan-OH (H-Glu-Trp-OH), hereafter abbreviated Trp-Glu and Glu-Trp, as potential anticancer agents against GBM through an integrated computational and experimental approach. Geometry optimization and electronic structure analyses were performed in Gaussian at the B3LYP/6-311 ++G(d,p) level. A conformational search over multiple starting geometries preceded optimization, and vibrational frequency calculations confirmed that all reported structures are true minima. Two reference states were used, each applied identically to both sequence isomers so that every comparison is strictly like-for-like. The electronic structure calculations and the ADMET predictions were carried out on the neutral form, which is the interpretable reference state for Koopmans-based reactivity descriptors and the input convention of the ADMET predictor; molecular docking and molecular dynamics were carried out on the anionic species that predominates at pH 7.4 (NH3 +, two COO-; net charge -1), which is the species that actually engages the binding sites. Molecular docking against six GBM-associated target proteins (CHI3L1-YKL-40/8R41, PI3K-alpha/4JPS, VEGFR-2/4ASD, IDH1 R132H/4UMX, STAT3/6NJS, and System xc-/7P9U) was performed using AutoDock Vina with grid-box centres, box dimensions, exhaustiveness, pose count and random seed reported in full; the protocol was validated by redocking each co-crystallized ligand into its own site and computing the heavy-atom RMSD against the crystallographic pose. Three targets (CHI3L1/YKL-40, VEGFR-2 and IDH1 R132H) were carried forward to 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in Schrodinger Desmond using the OPLS4 force field, one trajectory per complex, with both sequence isomers built in the same ionization state. Every docking calculation was repeated with five independent random seeds and is reported as mean +/- SD; the redocking validation was performed as a single run per target. No MM-GBSA binding free-energy estimation with per-residue decomposition. Comprehensive ADMET profiling was carried out using ADMETlab 3.0. In vitro anticancer activity was evaluated in U-87 GBM cells using the MTT assay at 10-100 μg/mL over 24, 48, and 72 h, with temozolomide as the reference agent; all concentrations are reported in both mass and molar units, and 72 h IC50 values with 95% confidence intervals were obtained by non-linear regression. In the corrected screen, every docking calculation was repeated with five independent random seeds and scores are reported as mean +/- SD. Glu-Trp gave the strongest score of the panel against CHI3L1/YKL-40 (8R41, -8.60 +/- 0.05 kcal/mol). Trp-Glu scored highest against CHI3L1/YKL-40 and VEGFR-2 (-8.19 +/- 0.24 and -8.17 +/- 0.02 kcal/mol), two values that are indistinguishable from one another. The two isomers ranked the six targets almost identically, but the difference between them lay within the seed-to-seed variability of the scoring function at only one of the six targets (System xc-, 0.08 +/- 0.21 kcal/mol); at the remaining five the separation exceeded that variability. VEGFR-2 was the exception of mechanistic interest: there the isomers occupied two distinct sub-pockets, Trp-Glu at the ATP-site hinge and Glu-Trp in the type-II back pocket, sharing no contact residue. Redocking of the co-crystallized ligand reproduced the crystallographic pose within the conventional 2.0 Å criterion for four of the six targets (VEGFR-2 0.54 Å, PI3K-alpha 0.62 Å, CHI3L1 1.02 Å, IDH1 R132H 1.20 Å), with STAT3 at 2.65 Å and System xc- at 3.91 Å. The HOMO-LUMO energy gap was 4.818 eV for Trp-Glu and 4.952 eV for Glu-Trp, a difference of 0.134 eV that is too small to be treated as evidence of differing biological activity. Molecular dynamics was extended from one target to three and each complex was simulated for 100 ns with both isomers in the same ionization state. The two sequences behaved differently, and in opposite directions at different targets. At VEGFR-2 Glu-Trp held its docked pose, with ligand RMSD confined to roughly 2-3.5 Å and hydrogen bonds to Glu885 and Arg1027 persisting for most of the trajectory, whereas Trp-Glu left its starting pose within the first 20 ns and settled into an alternative surface site anchored by Arg929 and Arg932. At IDH1 R132H the ordering reversed: Trp-Glu showed the smaller positional drift and a persistent hydrogen-bond network centred on Ile128, Ser287 and Ala282. At CHI3L1/YKL-40 Trp-Glu also relaxed out of its initial pose after approximately 65-70 ns; the Glu-Trp ligand of that system had been built without explicit bond-order information, so the Glu-Trp results at this target are reported as provisional and the comparison between the isomers there is not treated as quantitative. Each complex was simulated once rather than in replicate, and MM-GBSA free energies were not computed. ADMET profiling returned a mixed rather than a uniformly favourable picture: low predicted hERG and AMES liabilities, but one Lipinski violation (six hydrogen-bond donors), poor predicted Caco-2 and MDCK permeability, poor human liver microsome stability, very low predicted BBB permeability, and elevated nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity and genotoxicity probabilities. In the MTT assay, both dipeptides exerted negligible cytotoxicity at 24-48 h but produced marked, significant reductions in viability at 72 h. Trp-Glu displayed a monotonic concentration-response with its strongest effect at the highest concentration tested (100 μg/mL, 300 μM; IC50 82.9 μg/mL), whereas Glu-Trp displayed a non-monotonic concentration-response with its strongest effect at the lowest concentration tested (10 μg/mL, 30 μM). Because temozolomide was included as a single-concentration reference (100 μM, equivalent to 19.4 μg/mL) rather than as part of a dose-response series, the comparison is presented on a molar basis and no claim of superiority over temozolomide is made. Because Trp-Glu and Glu-Trp are sequence isomers of identical molecular formula and identical ionizable groups, every difference observed between them is attributable to residue order and to nothing else. On that controlled comparison the study makes one substantive finding, supported independently by two methods: sequence directionality changes where and how these dipeptides engage a protein. In docking it relocated the ligand between two distinct sub-pockets of VEGFR-2 with no contact residue in common, and in molecular dynamics it determined which isomer retained its initial pose, with the advantage reversing between VEGFR-2 and IDH1 R132H. The same directionality is visible in the cells, where the two isomers produced opposite concentration-response patterns at 72 h. The present work does not establish blood-brain barrier penetration, target engagement, mechanism of action or in vivo efficacy; the very low predicted BBB permeability and several elevated in silico toxicity flags are substantial liabilities. These dipeptides are therefore best regarded as starting structures whose sequence-dependent behaviour merits further mechanistic investigation, rather than as candidates ready for preclinical development.

title: Expanding a university-based social enterprise: organizational change across 15 years.
abstract: Social enterprises combine social purpose and commercial activity to address societal challenges, yet limited longitudinal evidence explains how they develop as they expand, particularly when operating within established institutions. This study examines the factors supporting expansion in a university-based social enterprise and how their function and importance change across stages of development. We conduct a 15-year longitudinal case study of an enterprise delivering substance use prevention to secondary school students through face-to-face and digital formats. Evidence includes trial and survey data, organizational records, governance and funding documentation, and an extensive body of peer-reviewed publications. Using a social innovation lens, the study examines the roles of university actors, schools, government, funders and industry across the expansion process. Expansion was accompanied by increasing interdependence between the enterprise and the university. The university provided credibility, expertise, resources and institutional support, while the enterprise contributed to the university's research activity and social mission. Technology also changed how work was coordinated as the organization developed. Initially embedded in the program offering, digital systems increasingly supported communication, collaboration, implementation monitoring and knowledge sharing across staff, schools, university actors and external stakeholders. As the enterprise expanded, roles and implementation processes became more structured, alongside greater requirements for technological oversight, security and accountability. This was important for replicability as the program introduced new platforms and expanded nationally. These findings show that social enterprise expansion involves reconfiguring the organizational systems and relationships through which social value is produced. The longitudinal perspective provides contextual and practical detail on how to achieve this for social enterprises working in a university setting.

title: Comparative analysis of SNPs associated with COVID-19 and chronic liver disease identifies DPP9 as a candidate genetic marker for Long COVID.
abstract: Long COVID is a multisystemic condition characterized by persistent symptoms after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, whose biological mechanisms are not yet fully understood. Host genetic factors may be associated, and the sharing of genetic architecture with other chronic diseases such as viral hepatitis B and C may aid in understanding this disease. A cross-sectional study was conducted including 150 individuals stratified into two groups: (i) Long COVID and (ii) chronic viral hepatitis B and C. Eighteen single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) previously associated with COVID-19 severity and inflammatory pathways were genotyped using TaqMan® real-time PCR assays. The analyses of genetic association models were performed using multivariate logistic regression adjusted for gender, self-reported skin color, and comorbidities. Mental health scales for assessing depression (Beck), anxiety (Hamilton), fatigue, and post-COVID functional scale were used both to define the syndrome and for subsequent analyses of the genotypic profile probably associated with Long COVID. Among all the SNPs analyzed, rs12610495 (A/G) in the DPP9 gene was the only variant consistently associated with Long COVID. After adjustment for sex, self-reported skin color, and hepatitis status, carriers of the G variant allele demonstrated increased odds of Long COVID under the dominant model (OR = 2.66; 95% CI: 1.08-6.57; p = 0.029) and the overdominant model (OR = 2.96; 95% CI: 1.17-7.52; p = 0.018). The association was more pronounced in women (OR = 3.30; 95% CI: 1.08-10.07). Exploratory analyses of mental and functional outcomes did not reach statistical significance, although a higher frequency of functional limitation and fatigue was observed among carriers of the G allele. This study suggests that DPP9 rs12610495 is associated with Long COVID, previously associated only with severe acute COVID, demonstrating that individuals carrying the rs12610495 G variant allele had higher odds of developing Long COVID. The inclusion of viral hepatitis as a chronic inflammatory condition for comparison contributed to the identification of shared genetic archetypal among diseases, revealing the possible role of DPP9 with Long COVID and highlighting this gene as a relevant target for future validation studies.

title: The effect of psilocybin on empathy and prosocial behavior: a proposed mechanism for enduring antidepressant effects
abstract: Psilocybin is a serotonergic psychedelic shown to have enduring antidepressant effects. Currently, the mechanism for its enduring effects is not well understood. Empathy and prosocial behavior may be important for understanding the therapeutic benefit of psilocybin. In this article we review the effect of psilocybin on empathy and prosocial behavior. Moreover, we propose that psilocybin may induce a positive feedback loop involving empathy and prosocial behavior which helps explain the observed, enduring antidepressant effects.

title: Do Large Language Models Walk Their Talk? Measuring the Gap Between Implicit Associations, Self-Report, and Behavioral Altruism
abstract: We investigate whether Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit altruistic tendencies, and critically, whether their implicit associations and self-reports predict actual altruistic behavior. Using a multi-method approach inspired by human social psychology, we tested 24 frontier LLMs across three paradigms: (1) an Implicit Association Test (IAT) measuring implicit altruism bias, (2) a forced binary choice task measuring behavioral altruism, and (3) a self-assessment scale measuring explicit altruism beliefs. Our key findings are: (1) All models show strong implicit pro-altruism bias (mean IAT = 0.87, p < .0001), confirming models "know" altruism is good. (2) Models behave more altruistically than chance (65.6% vs. 50%, p < .0001), but with substantial variation (48-85%). (3) Implicit associations do not predict behavior (r = .22, p = .29). (4) Most critically, models systematically overestimate their own altruism, claiming 77.5% altruism while acting at 65.6% (p < .0001, Cohen's d = 1.08). This "virtue signaling gap" affects 75% of models tested. Based on these findings, we recommend the Calibration Gap (the discrepancy between self-reported and behavioral values) as a standardized alignment metric. Well-calibrated models are more predictable and behaviorally consistent; only 12.5% of models achieve the ideal combination of high prosocial behavior and accurate self-knowledge.

title: Assessment of child self-regulation: A review of ecological and structured approaches
abstract: The extent to which developmental science has mapped associations between cognitive, academic and socio-emotional functioning; caregiver reports and non-participant observation of young children was examined. Initially, 88 studies comprising over 300 effects were identified. The relationships between outcome measures and research design was described. Findings show that recurrent associations between task performance, behavioral report and naturalistic observation appear in this literature. The most frequently occurring comparisons in school settings were those between children’s disruptive-aggressive behavior, on-task/off-task behavior, prosocial behavior, externalizing problems, prosocial skills and early math and language achievement. In home settings, those between children’s positive/negative affect, engagement, compliance, temperament, cognitive and motor development were most common. Despite conceptual overlap, limited access to correlational data and between-study heterogeneity hinders cross-sample comparisons.

title: MOOD AND EMPATHY ON PROSOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AMONG MUSLIM ADOLESCENTS IN PADANG CITY
abstract: This research is motivated by the phenomenon at the Dharmabakti Nusantara Health Vocational School in Padang City; mood and empathy are thought to influence prosocial behaviour. This study aims to analyse: 1) mood, empathy and prosocial behaviour, 2) the relationship between mood and prosocial behaviour, 3) the relationship between empathy and prosocial behaviour, and 4) the relationship between mood and empathy together with prosocial behaviour. The method used in this study is a Quantitative method that aims to determine the relationship and influence between variables. The research sample was taken from the existing population of 80 students. The research instrument used a questionnaire with a Likert scale model. The data were analysed with descriptive statistics, simple regression, and multiple regression; the results of the research data analysis obtained an R-value of 0.558 with a p level = 0.000 (p <0.05). There is a significant relationship between mood and empathy with prosocial behaviour. R2 =0,311 %. This study proves a positive and meaningful relationship between philosophy and heart in prosocial behaviour at SMK Dharmabakti Nusantara Pota Padang.

title: The Relationship between Well-Being, Empathy, Moral Identity, and Spirituality on Prosocial Behavior among Malaysian Youth
abstract: This study explores the influence of well-being, empathy, moral identity, and spirituality on prosocial behavior among Malaysian youth.A quantitative approach was employed with a sample of 411 participants, using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analyses to investigate the relationships between these variables.The results revealed that moral identity was the strongest predictor of prosocial behavior, followed closely by spirituality, empathy, and well-being.These findings highlight the central role of moral identity in shaping prosocial actions, with spirituality and empathy also playing significant roles.Well-being, while slightly less influential, still contributes meaningfully to prosocial behavior by promoting emotional stability and life satisfaction.The study emphasizes the importance of fostering moral development, spiritual growth, and emotional well-being to encourage prosocial behavior in youth.Policymakers, educators, and community leaders are encouraged to implement programs that focus on these key areas to promote a more compassionate and engaged youth population.

title: Nunca Solos: the multigenerational influence of dichos and moralejas on Latine adults
abstract: Dichos (sayings) and moralejas (stories with moral lessons) are important cultural traditions within Latine families that transmit values, knowledge, and life lessons across generations. While previous research has examined their use in educational settings and parenting programs, less is known about their long-term influence on the experiences of Latine adults. Guided by the Intergenerational Transmission of Cultural Socialization framework, this study explored (1) what dichos and moralejas Latine adults learned from their caregivers and (2) how dichos and moralejas support their current experiences as adults. Twenty Latine adults participated in semi-structured interviews conducted in English or Spanish. An inductive thematic analysis identified 72 dichos and moralejas participants learned from caregivers organized into seven categories: (a) work, effort, and perseverance; (b) character, conduct, and life lessons; (c) family, relationships, and identity; (d) caution, safety, and social behavior; (e) gratitude, humility, and generosity; (f) home and community interactions; and (g) time, opportunity, and fate. Participants described these teachings as shaping their work ethic, resilience, moral decision-making, social relationships, and family identity, while also providing examples of continued intergenerational transmission. Participants reported that the developmental impact of the dichos and moralejas increased when their meanings became clearer with the accumulation of life experiences. Findings highlight the role of dichos and moralejas as enduring cultural resources that support resilience, identity, and intergenerational continuity among Latine communities.
